content:
julia: Hit a nasty warmup stall when switching from 1-shard -> 4-shard safetensors bundles on low-memory nodes. Warmup waits for full index and then OOMs. Reproducer: /tmp/warmup-shard-stall.log

owen: This is the classic index-blocking problem. Two orthogonal fixes: (1) make loader non-blocking and support partial index entries, or (2) change shard layout to stream per-shard mini-index at start. Both have tradeoffs.

maria: I like incremental index entries because it keeps existing bundle formats. Proposed flow: transport emits index-fragments as they arrive. Loader exposes onIndexFragment(fragment) which can contain metadata for a subset of tensors. WarmupCoordinator can start prefix hydration for those entries immediately.

kevin: Implementation notes: fragments need stable IDs and a sequence number. Also add a fragment_watermark (default 48KB) to avoid thrashing on tiny fragments. If fragments don't cover critical layers within index_timeout (2s), fallback to full manifest fetch and throttle warmup to avoid OOM.

julia: We should also handle sharded quant tables: if quant table for a tensor isn't in fragment, warmup must request a lightweight quant-query RPC rather than blocking the whole tensor. That reduces tail latency.

owen: Telemetry: warmup.fragment_emitted, warmup.fragment_latency_ms, warmup.fallback_to_full_index, warmup.oom_protected_succeeds. Alerts: P95 fragment_latency_ms > 200ms or fallback rate > 0.5% in canary.

maria: Config sketch:

```yaml
loader:
  index_fragment_mode: enabled
  fragment_watermark_bytes: 49152
  index_timeout_ms: 2000
  fallback_policy: throttle_then_full_index
```

warmup-bot: Canary rollout: index-fragmenting v0.2 -> 1% canary started :rocket:

julia: I'll open a short RFC follow-up with state diagrams, fragment schema, and a compatibility test that simulates delayed fragment arrival. Aim to land adaptor + warmup coordinator changes in two sprints.

maria: +1. Also add unit tests for quant-table on-demand RPC path so we don't regress.

kevin: One more thought: consider opt-in producer hint header "fragment-first-supported" so new bundles can promise fragments early and avoid the fallback path entirely.
